module_title: Acoustic Pipes, Doppler Effect & Damped Systems (Advanced)
introduction: Tailored for high-yield JEE Advanced analytics and deep conceptual NEET items, this level analyzes organ pipes with end corrections, moving frames (Doppler Effect), and non-conservative damped oscillations.

core_concepts.title: Organ Pipes & Air Columns
core_concepts.description:
1. Closed Organ Pipe (one end closed): Produces ONLY odd harmonics ($f_1, 3f_1, 5f_1...$) where $f_1 = v/4L$. 
2. Open Organ Pipe (both ends open): Produces all harmonics ($f_1, 2f_1, 3f_1...$) where $f_1 = v/2L$.

core_concepts.title: Doppler Effect in Sound
core_concepts.description: The apparent change in frequency heard by an observer due to relative motion between the source and the observer. Apparent frequency: $f' = f \left( \frac{v \pm v_o}{v \mp v_s} \right)$, where $v$ is the speed of sound in air.

core_concepts.title: End Correction ($e$)
core_concepts.description: The reflection of air molecules doesn't happen exactly at the open plane but slightly outside it. For a pipe of radius $r$, the end correction per open end is $e \approx 0.6r$. Effective length for closed pipe is $L+e$; for open pipe, it is $L+2e$.

core_concepts.title: Damped Harmonic Motion
core_concepts.description: Occurs when dissipative forces (like air drag) drain energy from an oscillator. The amplitude decays exponentially over time: $A(t) = A_0 e^{-bt/2m}$, where $b$ is the damping constant.

important_entities.name: Harmonics vs. Overtones
important_entities.key_fact: Harmonics are integer multiples of $f_1$; overtones are physical frequencies above $f_1$.
important_entities.significance: In a closed organ pipe, the '3rd Harmonic' is simultaneously the '1st Overtone' because no 2nd harmonic ($2f_1$) physically exists in the system's spectrum.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The standard Doppler formula breaks down if: 1. The source or observer moves faster than the speed of sound ($v$). 2. The motion of the source/observer is exactly perpendicular to the straight line joining them (no relative component along the sound path).

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Approaching boosts frequency, receding drops it
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: In $f' = f \left( \frac{v \pm v_o}{v \mp v_s} \right)$, select your signs by checking relative behavior. If the observer or source moves to reduce the distance, choose signs that maximize the fraction (+$v_o$ in numerator, -$v_s$ in denominator).

exam_strategy_tips: In Resonance Column experiment problems, eliminate the troublesome end correction ($e$) entirely by subtracting the first two consecutive resonance lengths: $\lambda = 2(L_2 - L_1)$. Use this layout to resolve variables rapidly.
